Summary Description: Dr. Michael R. Sladek is a distinguished scholar in ethnic–racial identity (ERI) development, with a research program spanning daily-life processes of ERD, ERI, and EROC, and their implications for health and well-being. Grounded in the Phenomenological Variant of Ecological Systems Theory (PVEST), his work emphasizes integrative, longitudinal, and cross-cultural approaches, including US and Colombian contexts. His contributions include synthesizing daily-process literature to advance theory and health outcomes; empirical studies on ERI development across diverse contexts (notably Colombia and US classrooms); and the design and evaluation of education-focused interventions such as the Identity Project, which explore how teacher professional development can foster ERI exploration and culturally sustaining pedagogy. Across projects, his methodological portfolio blends qualitative (CQR, reflexive TA) and quantitative (SEM, LDS, mediation, multilevel modeling) approaches to test developmental cascades and inform classroom practice and policy.
